overall.sentence: The headline, local magnetic imaging of switchable orbital TRS breaking and chiral domains in the rhombohedral graphene superconductor, is new in method relative to the transport work of Han et al. [14] (arXiv:2408.15233), which shares question and system; no earlier paper with that imaging was found in the paper's references and 10 successful arXiv searches (2026-11-22).

assessment.claim: 1: SQUID-on-tip imaging of trainable, sign-reversible orbital magnetization in the R5G superconductor; magnetic evidence 'long sought but thus far absent'
assessment.note: Han et al. [14] reported TRS-breaking superconductivity with Rxx hysteresis in the same system by transport; new here is the local magnetic method. No earlier magnetic imaging of the superconductor found; Sheekey et al. (2605.30316) was posted after.

assessment.claim: 2: TRS breaking and chiral domains inherited from the quarter-metal parent
assessment.note: [14] already placed the superconductor inside the spin-valley polarized quarter metal with hysteresis in both; new is the imaged continuity of the domain structure.

assessment.claim: 3: domain-wall proliferation density coincides with superconducting onset, indicating a hidden transition
assessment.note: [8] reports a rotational-symmetry-breaking order intertwined with superconductivity and hysteresis in hexalayer RMG by transport; new is the n_DW coincidence in pentalayer and the domain-wall-energy picture.

assessment.claim: 4: 'first experimental imaging and estimate of the isospin DW resistivity in RMG' (~41 kOhm·µm)
assessment.note: [14] attributed resistance spikes to domain walls by transport in the same system; no earlier imaging or quantitative wall resistivity found.

assessment.claim: 5: sub-nA current moves domain walls, 'lowest ... reported to date'
assessment.note: SQUID imaging of current-driven domain reversal in a moire Chern magnet [46] and 1 nA switching in tBG [36] precede it; new is the system and the lower nominal onset current.

assessment.claim: 6: 'first realization of DW motion dominated by linear momentum transfer'
assessment.note: One targeted arXiv round found theory only (e.g. 0811.3545); too weak a search for no_precedent_found, and the paper's own [49] reports related behavior in permalloy.

assessment.claim: 'coexistence of superconductivity with oppositely polarized chiral domains has no analogue in any other superconductors'
assessment.note: Twisted MoTe2 [32] shows superconductivity inside a polarized anomalous Hall metal with hysteresis (transport); imaged domains are new here.

positioning: The paper sits directly on Han et al. [14], which found TRS-breaking superconductivity with magnetic hysteresis in the same system by transport, and on the group's own SQUID-on-tip imaging of the tetralayer quarter metal [16]; what it adds is real-space magnetic evidence in the superconducting state, imaged domain walls with a quantified resistivity, and current control of those walls. A closely overlapping nanoSQUID study (Sheekey et al., arXiv:2605.30316) was posted later in the same month and finds an orbital moment in a superconducting tetralayer and metastable domains, so referees may treat the two as concurrent. Sources: arXiv API (10 of 12 queries ran; two failed with HTTP 429 after retry: a broad chiral-superconductivity query, covered by later ones, and a query on SQUID imaging of moire Chern-magnet domains) and the paper's reference list.

closest.title: Signatures of Chiral Superconductivity in Rhombohedral Graphene
closest.overlap: Same question and system (TRS-breaking superconductivity from the quarter metal in rhombohedral tetra- and pentalayer graphene, with Rxx magnetic hysteresis); transport only, no magnetic imaging.

closest.title: Visualizing orbital magnetism in electron doped rhombohedral multilayer graphene
closest.overlap: Posted after this paper: nanoSQUID-on-tip magnetometry finding an orbital ferromagnetic moment in a superconducting rhombohedral tetralayer and metastable magnetic domains behind stochastic resistance switching.

closest.title: Stripe Order in the Metallic and Superconducting Phases of Rhombohedral Hexalayer Graphene
closest.overlap: Transport evidence of a rotational-symmetry-breaking (stripe) order coexisting with superconductivity and magnetism in rhombohedral hexalayer graphene, with hysteretic transitions tied to that order; cited as [8] under its later title.

closest.title: Visualizing isospin magnetic texture and intervalley exchange interaction in rhombohedral tetralayer graphene
closest.overlap: Same group and method (SQUID-on-tip imaging of isospin magnetization) in rhombohedral tetralayer graphene, but of the normal-state quarter and half metals, not the superconductor.

closest.title: Intrinsic spin Hall torque in a moire Chern magnet
closest.overlap: SQUID imaging shows current-driven reversal of individual magnetic domains in a moire Chern magnet (MoTe2/WSe2) at about 10^3 A/cm^2.

issues.claim: The density at which domain walls proliferate coincides with the onset of superconductivity, indicating a hidden transition in the parent state that both induces superconductivity and reduces domain-wall energy.
issues.headline: Hidden-order proposal omits cited stripe order in hexalayer superconductor
issues.issue: The proposed hidden symmetry-breaking transition that sets in with superconductivity is positioned only against C3 breaking in bilayer and trilayer graphene [15,69-71] and [72]. The paper's own reference [8] (arXiv:2504.05129, Qin et al. 2025) reports a rotational-symmetry-breaking stripe order coexisting with superconductivity in rhombohedral hexalayer graphene, with hysteretic transitions tied to that order, but is cited only for hysteresis and negative resistance. A referee from that community will ask how the hidden order here relates to it.

evidence.quote: This type of symmetry breaking has been observed experimentally in bilayer and rhombohedral trilayer graphene [15,69–71], and has recently been linked to the observation of an in-plane anomalous Hall response in RMG [72].
evidence.location: Methods, Suppression of DW energy by a hidden order

issues.fix: Add [8] to the hidden-order discussion (Methods and Discussion) and say whether the n_DW transition could be the stripe or anisotropic order reported there, and what distinguishes it.

edit.before: This type of symmetry breaking has been observed experimentally in bilayer and rhombohedral trilayer graphene [15,69–71], and has recently been linked to the observation of an in-plane anomalous Hall response in RMG [72].
edit.after: This type of symmetry breaking has been observed experimentally in bilayer and rhombohedral trilayer graphene [15,69–71], has recently been linked to the observation of an in-plane anomalous Hall response in RMG [72], and a rotational-symmetry-breaking stripe order coexisting with superconductivity and hysteretic transitions has been reported in rhombohedral hexalayer graphene [8].

prior.title: Stripe Order in the Metallic and Superconducting Phases of Rhombohedral Hexalayer Graphene
prior.overlap: Transport evidence of a rotational-symmetry-breaking (stripe) order coexisting with superconductivity and magnetism in rhombohedral hexalayer graphene, with hysteretic transitions tied to that order; cited as [8] under its later title.

issues.claim: Imaging of isospin domains and domain walls in strongly correlated 2D systems
issues.headline: Earlier SQUID imaging of orbital magnetic domains in graphene not cited
issues.issue: The introduction says domain walls in isospin-polarized, strongly correlated 2D systems remain largely unexplored, citing [35-37]. Tschirhart et al. 2020 (arXiv:2006.08053) used a SQUID to image micron-scale orbital magnetic domains and their field-driven reversal in twisted bilayer graphene on hBN, a valley-polarized graphene system, and is not cited. The paper cites the same group's later [46] and its own [42], so the gap is narrower than stated.

evidence.quote: In contrast, their counterparts in isospin-polarized and strongly correlated two-dimensional systems [35–37] remain largely unexplored.

issues.fix: Cite the earlier domain imaging in moire Chern magnets (arXiv:2006.08053, with [42] and [46]) and state the contribution as the first imaging of such domains and their walls across a superconducting transition.

edit.before: In contrast, their counterparts in isospin-polarized and strongly correlated two-dimensional systems [35–37] remain largely unexplored.
edit.after: In contrast, their counterparts in isospin-polarized and strongly correlated two-dimensional systems have been imaged only in moiré Chern magnets [35–37,42,46], and their properties remain largely unexplored.

prior.title: Imaging orbital ferromagnetism in a moiré Chern insulator
prior.overlap: SQUID imaging of micron-scale orbital magnetic domains and their field-driven reversal in twisted bilayer graphene/hBN, a graphene isospin (valley) polarized system.

prior.title: Intrinsic spin Hall torque in a moire Chern magnet
prior.overlap: SQUID imaging shows current-driven reversal of individual magnetic domains in a moire Chern magnet (MoTe2/WSe2) at about 10^3 A/cm^2.

issues.claim: Ultra-low currents, down to sub-nA, deterministically move domain walls and enable reversible switching between states of opposite chirality.
issues.headline: "Lowest current reported to date" compares unlike quantities
issues.issue: The 0.4 nA figure is the onset of resolvable wall motion at a nominal ac current, which Extended Data Table 1 says overstates the current in the sample, while the cited moire results are full switching currents: Serlin et al. (arXiv:1907.00261, [36]) switched orbital magnetic order with currents as small as 1 nA. The claim is not contradicted, but "to date" invites a referee to argue the comparison.

evidence.quote: Remarkably, DW dynamics can be resolved at currents as low as 0.4 nA (Extended Data Fig. 8g), representing the lowest magnetic domain manipulation current reported to date

issues.fix: Say the 0.4 nA is a nominal ac amplitude for the onset of wall motion and compare it with the 1 nA switching current of [36] explicitly, or soften to "among the lowest".

edit.before: Remarkably, DW dynamics can be resolved at currents as low as 0.4 nA (Extended Data Fig. 8g), representing the lowest magnetic domain manipulation current reported to date
edit.after: Remarkably, DW dynamics can be resolved at nominal currents as low as 0.4 nA (Extended Data Fig. 8g), among the lowest magnetic domain manipulation currents reported, below the ~1 nA switching currents in moiré Chern magnets

prior.title: Intrinsic quantized anomalous Hall effect in a moiré heterostructure
prior.overlap: Electrical currents as small as 1 nA switch the orbital magnetic order of twisted bilayer graphene/hBN; transport only.

prior.title: Intrinsic spin Hall torque in a moire Chern magnet
prior.overlap: SQUID imaging shows current-driven reversal of individual magnetic domains in a moire Chern magnet (MoTe2/WSe2) at about 10^3 A/cm^2.

issues.claim: Current-driven domain-wall motion is dominated by linear momentum transfer from reflected electrons, and both spin and valley contribute to the wall's barrier.
issues.headline: "First realization" of momentum-transfer wall motion rests on estimates
issues.issue: No earlier experiment matching this claim turned up in the arXiv searches, but the support is an order-of-magnitude force balance, and the paper's own reference [49] (Hayashi et al. 2007) reported wall velocities exceeding the spin-transfer rate in permalloy. "Indicate" plus "first realization" is stronger than the evidence needs.

evidence.quote: Our observations indicate that rhombohedral graphene provides the first realization of DW motion dominated by linear momentum transfer.
evidence.location: Methods, DW dynamics governed by linear momentum transfer

issues.fix: Drop "first" or qualify it, and say how this regime differs from the momentum-transfer contributions discussed for metallic ferromagnets [48,49].

edit.before: Our observations indicate that rhombohedral graphene provides the first realization of DW motion dominated by linear momentum transfer.
edit.after: Our observations indicate that DW motion in rhombohedral graphene is dominated by linear momentum transfer, a regime proposed theoretically [33,48] but, to our knowledge, not previously isolated experimentally.

prior.title: Current Driven Domain Wall Velocities Exceeding the Spin Angular Momentum Transfer Rate in Permalloy Nanowires
prior.overlap: Current-driven wall motion faster than spin transfer alone allows, in permalloy; title from the paper's reference list, not found in the arXiv searches.

issues.claim: SQUID-on-tip imaging of the zero-resistance state in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene shows a trainable, sign-reversible orbital magnetization, which the authors present as unambiguous evidence for chiral superconductivity.
issues.headline: "No analogue in any other superconductors" overlooks twisted MoTe2
issues.issue: Superconductivity inside a spin- and valley-polarized anomalous Hall metal with Hall hysteresis has also been reported in twisted MoTe2, the paper's own [32], as summarized in arXiv:2504.07082. Domains have not been imaged there, so the statement is not contradicted, but "any other superconductors" is broader than needed.

evidence.quote: Importantly, the coexistence of superconductivity with oppositely polarized chiral domains has no analogue in any other superconductors.

issues.fix: Narrow to imaged domains, and mention the twisted MoTe2 candidate [32].

edit.before: Importantly, the coexistence of superconductivity with oppositely polarized chiral domains has no analogue in any other superconductors.
edit.after: Importantly, directly imaged coexistence of superconductivity with oppositely polarized chiral domains has not been reported in other superconductors, including the candidate chiral superconductor in twisted MoTe2 [32].

prior.title: Chiral superconductivity from spin polarized Chern band in twisted MoTe$_2$
prior.overlap: Theory paper whose abstract summarizes the twisted MoTe2 experiment (this paper's [32]): superconductivity inside a spin/valley-polarized anomalous Hall metal with anomalous Hall hysteresis.
